title: The market for interfirm asset sales

rival_explanations: information hypothesis (bid conveys information that assets are undervalued; transfer of ownership not necessary to sustain the revaluation)
security-market inefficiency / prior undervaluation as the source of the revaluation, rather than movement of resources to higher-valued uses

context.sample_size: 55 successful sellers and 51 successful bidders; 59 unsuccessful sellers and 54 unsuccessful bidders; 49 voluntary liquidations

data_sources.name: Statistical Report on Mergers and Acquisitions (Federal Trade Commission)
Center for Research in Security Prices (CRSP) daily and monthly return files / stock master file
Mergers and Acquisitions ('Out the Window' section)
Standard and Poor's and Moody's annual dividend records

analyses.label: Table 2 - Daily stock price reactions to voluntary sell-off proposals (sellers and bidders, completed and terminated)
analyses.sample: 55 successful and 59 unsuccessful sellers; 51 successful and 54 unsuccessful bidders; 1963-1981

dv.name: abnormal returns (mean cumulative daily prediction errors)
dv.measure: Mean cumulative daily prediction errors (in percent) over various intervals; excess return PEjt = Rjt - (aj + bjRmt), market model estimated from day -400 to -201 relative to announcement, Rmt = equal-weighted CRSP index; standardized per Dodd-Warner (1983)
dv.source: Center for Research in Security Prices (CRSP) daily return files

key_ivs.name: voluntary sell-off (divestiture) proposal announcement
key_ivs.measure: two-day (-1,0) and five-day announcement-period return around the initial press announcement and the outcome (bid/termination) announcement; event dates from WSJ
key_ivs.source: The Wall Street Journal Index and WSJ; FTC Statistical Report

key_ivs.name: transaction success (completed vs terminated)
key_ivs.measure: subsample partition: successful sellers/bidders (FTC completed) vs unsuccessful sellers/bidders (Mergers and Acquisitions 'Out the Window' cancellations)
key_ivs.source: FTC Statistical Report; Mergers and Acquisitions

analyses.label: Table 3 - Unsuccessful sellers partitioned by presence/absence of a follow-up bid (information vs synergy hypothesis test)

dv.name: abnormal returns (cumulative daily prediction errors)
dv.source: Center for Research in Security Prices (CRSP) daily return files

key_ivs.name: presence of a follow-up (second) bid within two years of cancellation
key_ivs.measure: binary partition: firms with follow-up bid for the original target assets within two years vs firms without (30 without, 29 with)
key_ivs.source: The Wall Street Journal (press reports tracked for two years)

analyses.label: Table 4 - Monthly abnormal returns around voluntary liquidation announcements, partitioned by prior control bid
analyses.sample: 45 of 49 liquidating firms with sufficient monthly CRSP returns; 22 with control bids, 23 without; 1963-1983

dv.name: abnormal returns (monthly cumulative prediction errors)
dv.source: Center for Research in Security Prices (CRSP) monthly return files

key_ivs.name: presence of a control bid within two years before liquidation
key_ivs.measure: binary partition: firm involved in a control contest (merger proposals, tender offers, contests for board representation, leveraged buyout proposals) within two years prior vs not (22 with control bids, 23 without)
key_ivs.source: The Wall Street Journal press reports

analyses.label: Table 5 - Daily abnormal returns around voluntary total liquidations, partitioned by prior control bid
analyses.sample: 49 voluntary total liquidations; 24 firms with prior control bids and 25 without; 1963-1983

dv.name: abnormal returns (cumulative daily prediction errors)
dv.source: Center for Research in Security Prices (CRSP) daily return files

key_ivs.name: presence of a prior control bid within two years before liquidation
key_ivs.measure: binary partition: liquidations with prior control bids vs without (24 with, 25 without)
key_ivs.source: The Wall Street Journal press reports
